status: Concept art only; not dimensionally verified CAD or printable STL
common_prompt: Use case: stylized-concept / product-mockup. Create a polished industrial-design concept sheet for a fun FDM-3D-printable Keychain Kreatures virtual-pet handheld enclosure. The supplied PCB render is a LAYOUT REFERENCE, not a finished aesthetic: cover the electronics with the proposed shell. Respect its fixed component positions and scale. Main PCB is 96 mm wide by 105 mm tall; outer shell must be larger, a chunky almost-square portrait handheld, emphatically not a tiny keyfob or a thin phone. Show credible substantial side depth for socketed parts; exact depth is unverified. Small landscape 280x240 LCD at upper center, active area only about one third of overall device width, not a giant full-width screen. Give the small screen an attractive stepped bezel and a cheerful pixel-pet graphic. Below it: exactly FOUR separate direction buttons in a diamond at lower left, exactly FOUR action buttons in a diamond at lower right, and exactly ONE mode button between and slightly below them. NINE physical input buttons total, no joysticks or extra controls. Single round RGB lens to the upper right of the screen, in a raised protective pod allowing its tall socket. Two separate IR optical apertures at the top-left edge, one transmitter and one receiver. Do not hide those optics behind assumed IR-transparent printed plastic. PCB antenna at top center: no metal ornament, screw or rear battery in that region. Shell should look buildable as flat-backed front plate plus a deep rear tray with a visible parting seam, removable rear screw closure, simple captured button caps, and separately printed accent pieces. Small radiused or chamfered edges, broad durable features, no thin delicate appendages, no glue-only assembly or inaccessible snap hooks. FDM satin texture with subtle visible layer lines, not glossy injection-molded plastic. Color separation is separate solid-color printed parts, not detailed paint or multi-material gradients. Rear service access for the 50x50 power board on independent supports; show a single provisional charge USB-C opening on the rear lower region, a switch opening and small speaker grille, NOT a second external USB socket. Ports and rear board position are conceptual and must be checked in mechanical CAD. No invented electronics internals or dimensioned blueprints. White studio background. One large front three-quarter hero view and two smaller consistent supporting views: straight-on front and a rear three-quarter view. Keep the same shape, nine buttons and features in all views. Add only the short concept title and a small footer reading CONCEPT ONLY - FIT NOT VERIFIED. No unrelated logos or certification claims.

variants.title: 01 PIXEL POD
variants.prompt: Direction 1: simple cheerful retro capsule. Rounded rectangular main silhouette that can contain the entire rectangular PCB, flat front with bevel transitions, clean two-piece rear seam, a recessed contrasting face panel and a small robust side attachment eyelet. Playful two-tone filament color blocking, chunky friendly circular button caps with shallow directional marks. A small blocky speaker-slot motif gives character without making the LCD bigger. The restrained option: minimal decorative parts, easy student disassembly, no ears, no external arms or legs. Make it desirable like a well-designed hobbyist handheld, not a generic gray project box. Title: 01 PIXEL POD. Show the rear screw closure clearly in the smaller rear view.

variants.title: 02 CRITTER BUDDY
variants.prompt: Direction 2: a friendly creature-shaped handheld, with two broad short cat-like ear silhouettes integrated into the OUTER flat front-plate perimeter, outside the full rectangular PCB envelope. Ears are stout rounded triangular shapes, not thin protrusions; they can be printed in the plane of a flat panel. Subtle shallow cheek/whisker-like surface motifs and a contrasting belly/face insert make the toy feel like a pet without adding additional eyes, lights or buttons. The existing small screen remains the focus with a smiling pixel creature. Use lively contrasting solid filament colors in separate printed parts. Keep the rear tray relatively simple and screw removable, with a clearly visible seam. No dangling tail, no fragile whisker rods, no continuous organic undercuts. Title: 02 CRITTER BUDDY. The side view must still show generous real electronic volume, not a paper-thin toy.

variants.title: 03 TRAIL BOT
variants.prompt: Direction 3: playful little expedition robot / rugged field companion. A rounded-square, softly faceted outer bumper with broad chamfers and short grippy side ribs; do not cut into the rectangular PCB envelope. A removable contrasting front fascia and a deep rear equipment-tray silhouette, slightly more mechanical than the other concepts, with friendly proportions rather than weapon/tactical styling. Short diagonal speaker slots, bold solid-color accent buttons, sensible perimeter screw access, and a stout printed attachment eyelet outside the antenna zone. The lower rear can have a visually separate service panel; not a claim of a finalized battery door. Avoid tiny greebles, tall fins, metal antennae and decorative exposed electronics. Title: 03 TRAIL BOT. Show the same rear USB/switch service concept and nine-button layout as specified.
